title: Developer Experience: SDK guides, quickstarts & API examples — operating procedures and top support issues
author: Jordan Lee
body:
Overview

This page documents the Developer Experience (DevEx) playbook for SDK guides, quickstarts & templates, API examples, docs-site operating procedures, and the canonical list of top support issues + fixes. It is intended for technical writers, SDK owners, developer advocates, and on-call engineers who maintain developer-facing docs.

Goals
- Keep SDK guides and quickstarts consistent, accurate, and fast to consume.
- Reduce support load by shipping high-quality API examples and canonical fixes.
- Maintain an efficient docs publishing workflow with clear ownership and SLAs.

Scope
Applies to: Redwood public SDKs (python, js/ts, go), REST API examples, quickstarts (getting-started and integration templates), docs-site content and operating procedures hosted under eng-developer-experience.

Ownership and roles
- Docs owner: Developer Experience (DevEx) team (primary contact: Jordan Lee).
- SDK maintainers: individual SDK teams (python-sdk@redwood, ts-sdk@redwood, go-sdk@redwood).
- Reviewer pool: DevEx tech writers + SDK engineers.
- Support escalation: Customer Success -> DevEx -> SDK on-call.

Document types and canonical locations
1) SDK Guides (detailed): full API surface, auth patterns, error handling, pagination, rate limiting. Location: /eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates/sdk-guides.
2) Quickstarts & Templates (short): 5–15 minute 'get up and running' examples, plus integration templates (webhook, chat UI, embeddings). Location: quickstarts-and-templates.
3) API Examples: copy-paste code snippets for common tasks (text generation, chat, streaming, embeddings, function-calls). Embedded in SDK guides and separate examples page.
4) Docs-site Operating Procedures: CI/publish, versioning, translation, auditing. Location: docs-site.
5) Top Support Issues & Canonical Fixes: triage checklist and canonical text snippets/solutions used by Support and DevEx.

Standards for all docs
- Conversational, concise prose. Use complete sentences and clear headings.
- Each guide must include: purpose, prerequisites, quickstart (commands), configuration table, code example, troubleshooting, and related links.
- All code snippets must be runnable and tested on the latest SDK release before publishing.
- Use API stable names from the model catalog; include model version pinning examples.
- Add labels and metadata for searchability: language, quickstart-type, sdk-version.

Template: Quickstart (recommended structure)
- Title: <task> quickstart — <language>
- Short intro (1–2 sentences).
- Prerequisites (SDK version, API key, env vars).
- Install steps (commands).
- Minimal working example (copy-paste).
- Expected output snippet.
- Next steps (link to SDK guide).
- Troubleshooting (common failures).
- Ownership + last updated.

Example: Minimal JS Quickstart (text generation)
1) Prerequisites
- Node 18+
- @redwood-inference/sdk-js v1.3.0
- REDWOOD_API_KEY set in env

2) Install
- npm install @redwood-inference/sdk-js

3) example.js
- const Redwood = require('@redwood-inference/sdk-js');
- const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
- const resp = await client.text.generate({ model: 'rw-text-1', prompt: 'Write a haiku about low latency' });
- console.log(resp.text);

4) Expected output (example):
- A 3-line haiku about low latency.

API example conventions
- Use the official client constructor pattern for each language.
- Include both sync and streaming examples where applicable.
- Show error handling for transient (429, 5xx) and permanent (401, 403) errors.
- Always include a small snippet demonstrating model pinning and fallback policy configuration.

Docs-site operating procedures (publishing workflow)
1) Authoring
- Create a draft page in the quickstarts folder. Use the quickstart template.
- Run local docs preview: docs-site dev (or npm run docs:preview).

2) Testing
- For SDK code examples run language-specific test harness scripts: tests/examples/run_all.sh (python/js/go).
- Add CI step to run examples against a staging API key. Failure blocks merge.

3) Review and Approval
- Add two reviewers (one DevEx writer + one SDK engineer). Review checklist: accuracy, code runs, examples minimal, labels set, links valid.
- Merge only after approvals and successful CI.

4) Publishing
- Merges to main automatically trigger the docs pipeline and invalidate the CDN cache.
- Post-publish smoke test: open main quickstart and run the minimal example (within the allowed sandbox) — assigned to the PR author.

5) Versioning and archival
- Tag quickstarts with sdk-version metadata. When a breaking SDK change occurs, create new quickstart variant and mark old one archived with an explicit deprecation date.

Support SLAs for doc fixes
- Priority P0 (broken snippet preventing onboarding): Fix within 24 hours.
- P1 (incorrect guidance e.g., deprecated flag): Fix within 3 business days.
- P2 (improvement request): Triage during next content sprint.

Top support issues (canonical list & fixes)
1) Authentication failures (401 / API key errors)
- Cause: missing/invalid API key or environment variable not loaded in shells.
- Canonical fix: show export instructions and sample env debug command:
  - Bash: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_live_xxx
  - Node: console.log(process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY)
- Related doc: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates/auth-and-keys-quickstart.json

2) Streaming connection drops / partial responses
- Cause: client not handling backpressure or intermediate network timeout defaults.
- Canonical fix: include streaming reconnection patterns and recommended timeout 120s in example. Show pseudo-code for backpressure handling and graceful resume.

3) Rate limit (429) during load tests
- Cause: burst above account limits or missing batching.
- Canonical fix: recommend batching config in Redwood Optimize and example exponential backoff:
  - Retry policy: initial_delay=200ms, max_delay=10s, max_retries=6
  - Client code snippet with retry on 429 and jitter

4) Unexpected model output format for function/tool calls
- Cause: mismatched schema or function signature.
- Canonical fix: include explicit JSON Schema example, and show how to use the SDK's validateResponse utility: validateResponse(resp, schema).

5) Embeddings mismatch (different vector dims)
- Cause: calling embeddings from one model while evaluating against a different model.
- Canonical fix: document model family and dims table; always pin embedding model in examples.

6) Offline/Private deployment mismatches
- Cause: customer using private deployment with different model catalog.
- Canonical fix: quickstart addendum for Private: how to swap base_url and auth provider, plus a checklist: config, certs, and KMS access tests.

Canonical fixes: distribution and use
- Store canonical snippets in the canonical-snippets/ directory in the docs repo.
- Support answers must link to the canonical snippet and file a docs ticket if there are discrepancies.
- For each canonical fix, include a short test-case in tests/examples that reproduces the issue (or validates the fix).

Quality gates and CI checks
- All doc PRs must pass: spellcheck, link-checker, snippet-runner, and linter.
- Example runner must run against a staging API key and report failures to the PR.
- Weekly automated smoke-run of a sampled set of quickstarts (cron job) with results posted to the DevEx dashboard.

Metrics to track (DevEx KPIs)
- Time-to-first-success (TTFS): time for new user to complete a quickstart and run first successful example (target: < 15 minutes).
- Support-reduction: # of support tickets referencing doc issues (target: -25% YoY).
- Example-run success rate (CI): target 99% for latest stable quickstarts.

Maintenance cadence
- Content sprint every 2 weeks: prioritize SDK releases, top issues, and outstanding PRs.
- Quarterly audit: review all quickstarts for breaking SDK changes or deprecated APIs.

How to file a doc bug or improvement
1) Create a GitHub issue in the docs repo with label docs-bug or docs-improve and link to the Confluence page.
2) If the issue is P0/P1, ping #devex on slack and assign to the on-call devex engineer.

Cheat sheet: reviewer checklist (short)
- Does the code run and match current SDK semantics?
- Are prerequisites and installs explicit and minimal?
- Are failure modes and troubleshooting covered?
- Are labels, metadata, and related links included?
- Is ownership and last updated date present?

Appendix: Example CI snippet (yaml)
- name: Example-runner
  runs-on: ubuntu-latest
  steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4
    - name: Setup SDKs
      run: ./tests/examples/setup_all.sh
    - name: Run examples
      env:
        REDWOOD_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.REDWOOD_STAGING_KEY }}
      run: ./tests/examples/run_all.sh
